title: Covariance bound by the Fourier one-norm
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f,h$ be real-valued functions on the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, and let $\\varepsilon\\in\\mathbb R$. Suppose every nonempty set of at most $k$ coordinates has Fourier coefficient of $f$ with absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$, the Fourier degree of $h$ is at most $k$, and $\\varepsilon\\ge 0$. Then $|\\operatorname{Cov}(f,h)|\\le \\|\\widehat h\\|_1\\,\\varepsilon$, where the covariance and Fourier one-norm are taken with respect to the uniform measure on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f,h$ are real-valued functions on the sign cube
$f$ is Fourier-regular at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon$
The Fourier degree of $h$ is at most $k$
